check1_followup: All 18 check-1 findings were addressed in the text. The HaltModule rewrite (critical) is fixed: halt, lift, setUnlockAt, forcedTransferOverride and setDocument use A24's real functions, and R1 is raised against A15. The A15 dependency is now in app-graph.json. The cross-shape replay and cap-raise gaps, multisig proposer and allow-list binding, constructor seeding, handover table, on-chain revocation, named errors, id encoding, SGL+R rule, conflicted veto, kind-keyed onboarding, owned output path, vector harness, delay table, D04 principal test, OZ pin and upper-bound note are all fixed. The multisig fix introduced a new liveness defect (finding 3), and interfaces with A24, A26 and A27 that check 1 did not examine are still broken (findings 1, 2 and 5).

findings.issue: Operations that A24 and A28 define as several gateway calls under ONE approval id cannot run. A25 consumes a SINGLE id at first use and deliberately has no executeBatch. Four cases break. (a) Forced transfer or recovery on a paused token needs HaltModule.forcedTransferOverride(..., approvalId) and then forcedTransfer under the same id. A24 says so explicitly, so that OverrideConsumed proves both came from one approval. (b) A24's item 3a recovery sequence runs override, forcedTransfer, setAddressFrozen(new, true) and freezePartialTokens per token under one approval id. (c) A24 says A28 sends HaltModule.activate(compliance) with the first unpause under the same approval. activate is missing from A25's V2 allow-list and M09 list altogether, so no token can reach SM-06 active through the gateway. (d) The J09 route and V2 list still use recoveryAddress, which A24 item 3a says must not be called on shared storage (a test proves it fails for a holder of two trusts). The gateway also never checks that the approvalId argument inside forcedTransferOverride's calldata equals execute's approvalId.
findings.fix: Add a bounded, attested multi-call shape. For example, executeBatch(approvalId, Call[] calls, ...) with att.target = address(this) and att.dataHash = keccak256(abi.encode(calls)). Every inner call passes the kind/selector allow-list and the restrict-only rule, and the whole batch runs atomically and consumes the id once. Alternatively, use an ordered per-nonce SEQUENCE kind. Raise the dataHash definition with A15 as R7. Add HaltModule.activate to the V2 allow-list and the M09 list. Require the approvalId argument decoded from forcedTransferOverride calldata to equal execute's approvalId (OverrideApprovalMismatch). Replace recoveryAddress in the J09 route and test with A24's item 3a sequence, and keep recoveryAddress off the V2 list or mark it unused. Add challenges: a forced transfer on a paused token; unpause plus activate; a two-trust recovery. Each must succeed under one id, and replaying the batch must be refused.

findings.issue: A26's wallet contracts are not wired into the gateways or the multisig, so smart-wallet recovery (the primary J09 path) and the D04 on-chain kill switch for investor agents' session keys cannot work in deployment. A26 names the V2 gateway as RealXGuardianRegistry.guardian and the V3 gateway as revoker. A26 lists the selectors A25 must allow-list. On V2: RecoveryModule.proposeOwner, cancelProposal and executeRecovery, SessionKeyModule.revoke and revokeAll, and RealXGuardianRegistry.pauseSessionKeys and unpauseSessionKeys. On V3: revoke, revokeAll and pauseSessionKeys. A26 also makes the V1 multisig the owner of the registry (setGuardian, setRevoker, Ownable2Step) and of the paymaster (addTarget, removeTarget, setCaps, setSigner). A25 has only four target kinds (TOKEN, HALT_MODULE, LOCKIN_MODULE, DOCUMENT_ANCHOR). Its V3 constructor accepts exactly four pairs. Its V1 list has none of these setters, and A26 is not a dependency. A27 expects a gateway Executed whose target is the RecoveryModule, which can never happen.
findings.fix: Add A26 as a dependency of A25 in app-graph.json and the note. Both are AM2, and A26 depends only on A07, so this makes no cycle. Add target kinds RECOVERY_MODULE, SESSION_KEY_MODULE and GUARDIAN_REGISTRY, with selectors taken from A26's wallet.json and ABIs, never typed by hand. Extend V3's restrict-only set to revoke, revokeAll and pauseSessionKeys, and add unpauseSessionKeys, proposeOwner and executeRecovery to V3's never-allowed list. Add the registry and paymaster owner setters, and A26's acceptOwnership, to the V1 allow-list and the delay table. Extend 30-handover.ts and 40-verify.ts to cover A26's slots: registry guardian = V2, revoker = V3, owner = multisig; paymaster owner = multisig. Add J09 smart-wallet recovery and a D04 'V3 revokes an agent session key' test through the real gateways.

findings.issue: The multisig rule 'the proposer can never approve', combined with 'the maker can never approve', turns the product map's V1 3-of-5 into 4 owners acting on every change, and 5 of 5 when the maker is an owner who did not propose. An example is the product map's 'Change signer policy' row, where SECO, a V1 owner, is the maker. With two owner keys lost or compromised (the case a 3-of-5 is meant to survive), the three remaining owners can never reach threshold: one must propose and cannot approve, leaving 2 approvers. The owner-replacement proposal itself then cannot pass, so V1 is bricked permanently: no owner rotation, no gateway signer rotation, no upgrade. The spec's claim that 'at least three eligible approvers' remain holds only when all five keys are live, and no challenge tests key loss.
findings.fix: Count the proposer's proposal as their approval unless proposerId == makerId. The maker is then the only excluded owner, and any three non-maker owners can act, which matches the product map's 3-of-5 and A15's off-chain 'P9 applied'. Alternatively, let a non-owner relayer submit a proposal that carries A15's V1 attestation. Add liveness challenges: with two owner keys unavailable, the remaining three replace an owner after 48 h; with the maker an owner, the three non-maker owners pass it. Record the chosen rule as founder-visible.

findings.issue: The V1 allow-list and denylist leave a second, unattested route for gateway-only operations. callModuleFunction is on the V1 list, but its inner calldata is not decoded. The hard denylist covers only Token agent functions. setAllowedSelector can add any selector not on the denylist. A24 makes lift, activate, forcedTransferOverride and setUnlockAt callable by the compliance owner (the multisig), and DocumentAnchor.setDocument by the token owner. So the multisig can lift halts, arm forced-transfer overrides and change lock-ins with no attestation or approval-id binding. M09's 'exactly one allow-listed route' criterion could still pass, because a test only diffs allow-list tables.
findings.fix: Make the multisig denylist the union of every selector on the V2 and V3 allow-lists (generated from the ABIs), including the A26 wallet selectors and HaltModule/LockInModule/DocumentAnchor functions. For callModuleFunction, decode the inner selector and allow only module configuration setters (setHalter, setLifter, module parameter setters), else ValueMovingSelector. Add challenges: propose callModuleFunction(lift), a direct HaltModule.lift, and setAllowedSelector(setUnlockAt). Each must revert.

findings.issue: The event contract with A27, the direct child that indexes these logs, does not match, and no reconciliation item covers it. A27 joins the multisig Executed(id, approvalId) to a stored Proposed(id, approvalId, target, selector, dataHash, makerId). A25 emits Proposed(id, approvalId, proposerId, makerId, callsHash) over a batch of up to 16 calls. A27's decode table omits ApprovalRevoked and TargetKindSet, and A27 raises chain.indexer_inconsistent on any undecodable manifest topic, requiring the count to be zero. As written, V1 ops can never be matched and every revocation trips an alert.
findings.fix: Add reconciliation item R7 (A27): A27 matches V1 ops on callsHash (keccak of the abi-encoded Call[]), or A25 additionally emits one ProposedCall(id, index, target, selector, dataHash) per call. A27 adds ApprovalRevoked and TargetKindSet (and any new A26-kind events) to its decode table and binds ApprovalRevoked to the CustodyOp veto. Add a test in A25 that an independent viem decoder parses every A25 event using A27's published event table.

findings.issue: D04's rule that segregation of duties counts an agent as its human is not carried on-chain, and the no-agent-signer rule is checked only at deploy time. The spec defines makerId as keccak of 'the A11 staff principal id' but never says what it is when an AGNT staff agent is the maker in A14. If A15 puts the agent's own principal id there, the human behind the agent can sign their own agent's op and MakerCannotSign never fires. Also, 40-verify.ts checks signers against the fixture once, but later addSigner or owner-change proposals can seed an AGNT, AGT-U or SVCA principal without any check. A zero makerId would exclude nobody.
findings.fix: State that for an agent-made op, makerId = keccak256 of the on_behalf_of human's principal id, never the agent's. Add it to R4 for A15, with a vector where an AGNT maker's human signs and must revert MakerCannotSign. Refuse makerId == 0 in execute and propose (MakerRequired). Add a reconciliation item for A27 or A15: every SignerAdded or owner-change event is checked against A11 principal types, and a non-staff principal raises a Sev1. Also add a multisig challenge that proposes addSigner with an AGNT principal id and expects the off-chain refusal.

findings.issue: Graph and summary drift. app-graph.json lists A25 as unlocking A27 and A106 (A106 uses 'the multisig signer-set selector'), but the note's Unlocks line names only A27. The Depends line still calls A15 'a pending graph reconciliation', although app-graph.json already carries the edge (only final-graph.json lacks it). The node summary says 'about 200 lines of custom Solidity', while the spec budgets 400 and escalates only past 400.
findings.fix: Add [[A106 - IAM admin API for ADM-37]] to Unlocks. Reword the A15 note so the edge is in app-graph.json and final-graph.json is to be regenerated. Update the node summary to '400 lines at most (gateway about 220, multisig about 180)', or tighten the spec back toward 200.

findings.issue: A MINT approval id is not bound to one target. Later chunks may carry attestations for a different token under the same id and cap. The spec defends against a later attestation raising the cap (CapMismatch), which assumes the same threat model, so the target should be locked the same way. Also, the design reference names a 'TokenOpRow' that does not exist in RealX App.dc.html (the adToken rows are an sc-for over tokenOps printing '{{ o.id }} · {{ o.appr }}'). The SM-00 mapping omits broadcast → failed (a gateway revert).
findings.fix: Record targetOf[approvalId] at first MINT use and refuse a different target (TargetMismatch), with a challenge. Refer to the design element as 'the adToken tokenOps row (o.id · o.appr)'. Add 'a named revert maps to SM-00 failed' to the SM-00 done criteria.
